key_insight: StraTA injects a compact, explicit trajectory-level strategy into agentic RL so that an LLM-based agent plans at the strategy level before acting, greatly improving exploration and credit assignment over long horizons.
problem_solved: Current LLM agents are largely reactive and struggle with long-horizon decision making because they lack explicit trajectory-level planning, which weakens exploration and makes credit assignment across extended trajectories difficult.
method: Sample a compact trajectory-level strategy (an abstract plan or latent) at episode or segment start to guide downstream decisions.
Condition the agent’s action policy on the sampled strategy so low-level actions are coherent with a higher-level intent while preserving flexibility.
Train the abstraction and policy jointly under a reinforcement objective so strategies improve exploration and long-horizon credit assignment.
impact: Provides a simple, model-agnostic way to make LLM agents more strategic—boosting long-horizon performance and more reliable exploration—useful for practitioners building complex agentic systems or hierarchical RL pipelines.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: two-level flow showing 'Strategy sampler' -> 'LLM agent conditioned on strategy' -> environment actions
Timeline comparison: reactive vs StraTA showing better exploration and clearer credit assignment across long trajectories
Performance chart: episodic return or success rate vs episode length comparing baseline reactive agents and StraTA
Icon set: strategy token / plan, action-level policy, environment/trajectory to convey hierarchy
paper_title: StraTA: Incentivizing Agentic Reinforcement Learning with Strategic Trajectory Abstraction
paper_authors: Xiangyuan Xue, Yifan Zhou, Zidong Wang, Shengji Tang, Philip Torr
